name: Pale Taupe
lede: Pale Taupe is ColorHub's English name for Gin-nezumi, a light warm grey that Japanese tradition names "silver mouse," one of a large family of named greys built on the word for mouse.

sections.title: Silver, and a mouse
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Gin-nezumi (銀鼠), literally "silver mouse": gin names the metal's pale sheen, and nezumi ("mouse") marks it as one of a family of muted greys graded by how dark or light the mouse coat runs [1]. ColorHub's English rendering, Pale Taupe, keeps the warmth but drops the silver and the mouse [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places the swatch in block 63, "light brownish gray," about 2.9 units from that block's centre[2]. The library's nearest other named color is [[warm-grey]], 2.5 units away [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 57, chroma 9, hue 59 degrees, light and only mildly warm [2]. At that lightness the color reads as a pale neutral on most screens, closer to the "silver" half of its Japanese name than to any mouse-dark shade [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 1,455 of 23,781 paintings, about 6 percent, as photographed [3]. Unusually for a grey this light, it plays a highlight role slightly more often than a mid-tone, 51 against 39 percent, and is rarely a shadow [3]. The Chinese painter Xugu carries it at more than ten times the archive's overall rate [3]. It shares canvases more than chance with the color words Silver and [[taupe]], and its presence peaks in the 1460s, in 10 of 71 paintings [3].
